title: Open detail D1d · What the button that changes nothing says when nothing would be lost
subtitle: From item 8; for Main's shared confirm box. Item 8 made the button that changes nothing say what stays (“Keep payment”, “Keep student” …). Four asks lose nothing even if the action goes ahead, so item 8 didn't settle them: Forms' “Open kiosk mode on this device?” and “End kiosk mode on all tablets?”, and Prospects' box when a Board card is dropped on Came (“Did … come to the free class?”, or “… 's free class is still ahead” before the class day). All four say “Cancel”. Two can be misread: next to “End kiosk mode”, “Cancel” can read as “cancel kiosk mode” — the same as the action; under “Maya's free class is Mon, Oct 26”, a lone “Cancel” can read as “cancel her class” (Prospects also has a real “Cancel booking” button). On phones Prospects' Came box shows only “Came” (the back arrow closes it). (Preview screenshots · PC size · fake data)

columns.note: The rule in B: every “are you sure?” box — including the ones that lose nothing — names what stays: “Keep …” for a thing, “Stay …” for a place. “Cancel” stays the word in form dialogs, where it throws away the typing (Cancel · Save). The first focus stays as decided in D1c: on the action in these four, since nothing is lost. Pictures 5–8 are drawn over the real boxes; nothing in the app was changed.

footer:
Your choice — one question: what should the button that changes nothing say in these four asks?
A · Keep “Cancel” here. Item 8's “Keep …” covers only boxes where something is changed or lost; these four are written down as the exception. + no work; “Cancel” is the word most apps use. − pictures 2 and 4 can be misread; two different words for the same button across the dashboard.
B · Recommended: say what stays (pictures 5–8). “Stay in the dashboard”, “Keep kiosk mode on”, “Keep in Booked” (the card's column). + one rule in every box; nothing to misread; matches the leave warnings' “Stay on this page”. − longer labels (on small phones they stack, D1b); four labels change (Forms, Prospects).
C · One plain phrase: “Go back” in all four. + short; one phrase to learn; can't be read as cancelling something. − doesn't say what stays; a second pattern next to “Keep …”.
